Debug Overlay v3.8.127 — clean build

This is the no-updater build — probably not the one you want. It has no update button and no options page, on purpose. If you want one-button updates, download debug-overlay-extension.zip instead: same overlay, plus an update screen. Use this build only if your antivirus objects to that one.
Why it exists: a program that downloads files and writes them to disk resembles a downloader, and on some machines it gets quarantined — which deletes the files and makes Chrome drop the extension. Nothing here fetches, writes to disk, or reloads itself, so there is nothing to quarantine. This page only tells you where to click.
Step 1 — you already did this.
You extracted the ZIP this page came from. Keep that folder somewhere permanent — not Downloads, not a temp folder — because Chrome will read it every time it starts.
Step 2 — open the extensions page.
A web page is not allowed to open it for you. Copy the address and paste it into the address bar:

chrome://extensions (Edge: edge://extensions)
Step 3 — the two clicks the browser requires from a human.
On that page: switch ON Developer mode (top-right), press Load unpacked, and select the folder from Step 1 — the one this page is inside of.
Step 4 — use it.
Open any website and press Alt+Shift+D for the on-page panel, or click the Debug Overlay button in the toolbar for the side panel.
Getting updates.
There is no update button in this build, on purpose. Download the newer ZIP, extract it over this same folder, then press the ↻ reload icon on chrome://extensions.
Once this is published to the Chrome Web Store, installing becomes one click and updates happen by themselves — no folder, no Developer mode, nothing to extract.
